title: Buying Off-Plan Property in Phuket: How It Works and Risks
description: How off-plan condo buying works in Phuket: payment schedules, completion dates, renders vs finished units and the checks to make before you reserve.
sub: Pre-sale and under-construction projects: benefits, risks and checks
intro: Off-plan means you buy a unit before the building is finished. Many new Phuket projects are sold this way. It can give access to a lower entry price and a choice of units, and it also carries construction and delay risk. This guide explains how it works and what to verify.

sections.h2: What counts as off-plan in our catalogue
p: Projects marked Pre-sale have launched sales before or at the start of construction. Under construction projects are being built. Completed projects are finished and can be viewed. At the moment {n_offplan} of our {n_projects} catalogue projects are pre-sale or under construction, and {n_completed} are completed.

A typical structure is a booking fee, a deposit when you sign the sale and purchase agreement and then instalments tied to construction stages, with a final payment at completion and transfer. Our standard reference is a THB 100,000 booking fee, 20% on contract signing and the remaining 80% in construction-linked instalments, but every developer sets its own plan. We show a developer’s own plan on the project page when we have it.

sections.h2: Advantages and risks, side by side
ul: Advantage: wider unit choice and often a lower entry price than a finished comparable unit.
Advantage: payments are spread over the build period.
Risk: delays. The completion date shown is the developer’s advertised target, not a guarantee.
Risk: the finished building may differ from renders and show-unit photos.
Risk: you hold a contract, not yet a title, until transfer.
Risk: developer financial strength matters more when you pay before you can see the product.

sections.h2: What to check before you reserve
ul: Developer history: completed projects and how they performed against their dates.
Land title and building permits for this project, checked by your lawyer.
Contract clauses: delay compensation, termination and refund, what happens to your deposit.
Payment protection: ask how construction-linked payments are tied to verified progress.
Foreign quota availability for the unit you want.
Specification list: finishes, furniture, parking, facilities and when they will open.

p: Ask for dated construction photos and, if you are abroad, periodic site updates. Compare them with the schedule in the contract.

If you want certainty about what you buy and a fast handover, a completed unit is simpler. If you want a lower entry price and can accept the wait, off-plan can fit. Both are available in our catalogue; you can filter by construction status in Sale and New Projects.

faq.a: No. It is the developer’s target. Your contract should state delay remedies.
Some contracts allow assigning your rights, some restrict it, and developers may charge a fee. Check the contract and ask your lawyer.

faq.q: Are the photos on project pages real?
faq.a: Many are developer renders for projects not yet built. Where we know images are renders, the project page says so.
